offerings.name: Willow Wreath
offerings.description: One of the hardest things to make with willow is a wreath. It takes time to develop the intuition needed to bend it from a straight whip into a perfect circle. Would you like to try your hand at this ancient holiday tradition?
offerings.note: Participants receive enough willow for four wreaths, 8 to 12 inches across. We weave three together and the fourth bundle goes home. Available 1 November to 31 March.

offerings.name: Moon and Star
offerings.alt: A woven willow moon and star
offerings.description: An invitation to explore what willow can do. We talk about where to find it in Alberta, how to harvest it responsibly, and how to dry, store, and soak it so it is ready to weave months later. Everyone leaves with a moon and a star, and a better sense of the material.
offerings.note: Can run as one workshop, or as two consecutive sessions with stars in the first and a larger moon in the second. Both together need five hours and cost $145.

offerings.name: Berry Boat
offerings.alt: A shallow woven willow berry boat
offerings.description: A boat of willow knows many voyages. It can wander into the brambles to gather berries, sit on the table holding crackers, or rest quietly on a shelf cradling tiny treasures. After a short tutorial, everyone shapes their own boat over a small jig.

offerings.name: Suet Bird Feeder
offerings.alt: A woven willow suet bird feeder
offerings.description: A suet feeder from locally harvested willow, and a good first project for anyone curious about natural materials but not ready for a whole basket. We cover willow itself, and a weave called pairing.
offerings.note: Price includes two pieces of suet.

offerings.name: Tiny Trug
offerings.description: Together we will shape a tiny willow trug, a small basket made to cradle soft petals, fragrant herbs, and the delicate treasures that whisper from the forest floor.

offerings.name: Cattail Berry Basket
offerings.alt: A berry basket woven from cattail leaves
offerings.description: What if the rustling cattails that line the marshes could be coaxed into carrying your berries home? Join us to find out, as we turn green blades into a small vessel for gathering summer’s sweetest moments. We weave cattail over a wooden form, practising the checkerboard weave, pairing, and waling, and finish with a simple trac border.

offerings.name: Textured Willow Bowl
offerings.alt: A textured willow bowl woven in rope coil
offerings.description: A textured bowl using a rope coil weave. We start with a 3 x 3 slath base, then weave a 4-rod drop-down wale to create a slight foot before moving up the sides. Once it clicks, this weave moves quickly. Finished with a rod border.

offerings.name: Berry Basket
offerings.alt: A small round willow berry basket
offerings.description: A small round willow basket, and the best of the beginner projects. The basics of stake and strand basketry: a slath base, waling, pairing, slewing, and a rod border, with an optional wrapped-core handle.

offerings.name: Large Round Willow Basket
offerings.alt: A large round willow basket with inset handles
offerings.description: Over two days we weave a generous round basket and the core techniques underneath it: a 3 x 3 slath base, pairing, waling, and French randing, finished with a classic rod border and optional inset handles.
offerings.note: Two days gives the time to work deeply with willow, to find the rhythm of it, and to carry home a basket built to serve for years.

offerings.name: Large Twisted Willow Basket
offerings.alt: A large sculptural willow basket with a twisted rope effect
offerings.description: Two full days shaping a sculptural willow basket. This project is big, bold, and deeply satisfying to create, a basket that shows off the natural strength and beauty of willow. We work with generous bundles of material to build a striking twisted rope effect.
offerings.note: Along the way: pairing, waling, and rod borders, with the option of a sturdy handle.
